findings.title: Multiple autoantibodies preceded a higher risk of diagnosis
findings.summary: Among children at increased genetic risk, the first detection of several islet autoantibodies identified a group more likely to develop T1D over the next decade.
findings.population: 585 children with multiple antibodies (median age at detection 2.1 years); 474 with one (median 4.8).
findings.factor: Two or more distinct islet autoantibodies
findings.followup: Ten-year estimates after seroconversion; median observation 4.5 vs 5.5 years.
findings.effect: 69.7% vs 14.5% ten-year risk.
findings.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals 65.1–74.3% and 10.3–18.7%.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: Selected birth cohorts. The analysis cannot establish that antibodies caused cell loss. Glucose stage at first detection was not required.
findings.locator: Abstract, Results; Figure 2 and Results subsections for multiple vs single antibodies.

findings.title: An HLA genotype predicted faster progression
findings.summary: Among children who developed multiple autoantibodies, the DR3/DR4-DQ8 genotype was associated with earlier diagnosis.
findings.population: 585 children with multiple islet autoantibodies; median age at detection 2.1 years.
findings.factor: HLA DR3/DR4-DQ8
findings.effect: Adjusted hazard ratio 1.35; ten-year risk 76.6% vs 66.2%.
findings.uncertainty: 95% CI for the hazard ratio 1.09–1.68.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: An association after autoimmunity begins does not identify the initiating event. The same children contribute to the autoantibody finding.
findings.locator: Table 2, HLA genotype row; adjustment includes age at seroconversion, sex and antibody count.

findings.title: Islet-reactive T cells were visible inside inflamed islets
findings.summary: Staining located CD8 T cells that recognized islet proteins in selected donor pancreases, in some cases years after diagnosis.
findings.population: 45 T1D donors; the 11 intensively studied cases were aged 5–26. Additional control groups included 14 donors without diabetes.
findings.factor: CD8 T-cell recognition of islet antigens, including insulin
findings.followup: One tissue collection per donor; positive cases up to 8 years after diagnosis.
findings.effect: Direct localization in selected islets.
findings.uncertainty: No population effect estimate or confidence interval.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: Tissue collected after diagnosis cannot date initiation or demonstrate that a cell killed its target. Antigen testing selected compatible samples with inflammation.
findings.locator: Figure 3, A–I (islet specificity and mismatched control); Table 1 (ages).

findings.title: Some donors retained insulin-containing cells without detectable C-peptide
findings.summary: The donor survey found residual beta cells in six longstanding cases without detectable local infiltration or HLA class I upregulation.
findings.population: Six longstanding insulin-positive cases; ages of this subset not summarized in the cited paragraph.
findings.factor: Insulin staining in residual beta cells
findings.comparator: Donors with inflammation and insulin-positive cells
findings.endpoint: Tissue insulin, circulating C-peptide and local immune infiltration
findings.effect: Only 2 of 5 tested had detectable C-peptide; the sixth value was unavailable.
findings.uncertainty: Small descriptive subset; no interval reported.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: A tissue snapshot cannot recover earlier immune attacks. Staining cannot tell whether enough insulin was released to affect glucose control.
findings.role: Counterevidence · tissue and function can diverge
findings.locator: Results immediately before “Multifocal islet autoimmunity”; Figure 1 I–L; Table S1.

findings.title: Persistent enterovirus B shedding preceded islet autoimmunity
findings.summary: Children repeatedly shedding the same enterovirus B strain had higher odds of later confirmed islet autoimmunity.
findings.population: 383 matched case/control pairs in TEDDY; children at genetic risk, at least 6 months old at sampling.
findings.factor: Same EV-B strain detected over more than 30 days
findings.followup: Monthly stool collection at 3–48 months; quarterly thereafter through age 10.
findings.effect: Odds ratio 2.50.
findings.uncertainty: 95% CI 1.19–5.26. Single positive samples had OR 0.69 (0.45–1.06).
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: Host immune differences may influence both shedding and risk. Stool does not show infection of the pancreas.
findings.locator: Figure 3, HLA-adjusted estimate for prolonged same-serotype EV-B shedding.

findings.title: The clinical diabetes analysis left substantial uncertainty
findings.summary: The authors did not establish an association between prolonged same-strain shedding and clinical T1D in their smaller diagnosis analysis.
findings.population: 112 matched pairs of genetically susceptible children; 93 autoimmunity cases also appeared in this analysis.
findings.factor: Prolonged shedding of one EV-B serotype
findings.comparator: Matched controls without diagnosed T1D at case diagnosis
findings.followup: Stool sampled during childhood before the matched event.
findings.effect: 8 cases and 2 controls had prolonged same-serotype shedding.
findings.uncertainty: At 10% exposure, 80% power required an odds ratio above 4.58, versus 2.28 for autoimmunity.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: Different endpoint and partly overlapping participants; the smaller analysis leaves moderate effects unresolved.
findings.locator: T1D results (paragraph on eight cases); Methods, nested matched case–control population, power calculation.

findings.title: A pooled shedding result partly reused TEDDY participants
findings.summary: A review combined three stool studies of consecutive enterovirus detection, including Vehik’s TEDDY study. The definition allowed any enterovirus in sequential samples.
findings.population: Children ≤18 across the review; three stool studies for this estimate.
findings.factor: Enterovirus in at least two consecutive stool samples
findings.comparator: Children without islet autoimmunity matched within the original studies
findings.followup: Follow-up and sampling differed by cohort.
findings.effect: Pooled odds ratio 1.55.
findings.harms: No treatment assigned in this analysis.
findings.limitation: The review includes TEDDY. Consecutive detection alone does not establish persistence of the same EV-B strain.
findings.role: Evidence synthesis · includes a selected primary study
findings.locator: Results §3.3 and Figure 5; Table 1 identifies Vehik’s TEDDY cohort.

findings.title: A T-cell clone killed compatible human islet cells in culture
findings.summary: A preproinsulin-reactive CD8 T-cell clone damaged human islet cells carrying HLA-A2. HLA-mismatched islets and a clone targeting a viral protein provided specificity controls.
findings.population: Human donor islets and a T-cell clone derived from a person with T1D. Donor ages not specified for this assay.
findings.factor: Preproinsulin recognition by the 1E6 clone
findings.comparator: HLA-A2-negative islets and a virus-specific CD8 T-cell clone
findings.endpoint: Islet cell lysis and insulin vs glucagon gene expression
findings.followup: Four-hour cell killing assay; no clinical follow-up.
findings.effect: Islet cell killing required matching HLA. Insulin mRNA fell more than fourfold versus cultures without the clone.
findings.uncertainty: Cell killing is plotted by cell ratio; no clinical effect or interval estimated.
findings.harms: No treatment administered to a person.
findings.limitation: The researchers stimulated islets with cytokines before testing. A selected clone under these conditions cannot establish whether this pathway initiates T1D in people.
findings.role: Experimental perturbation · human cells in culture
findings.locator: Figure 5B–C; Methods, human islet isolation and cytotoxicity assay.

findings.title: Teplizumab delayed clinical diagnosis
findings.summary: After one course targeting CD3 on T cells, relatives at high risk reached stage 3 later.
findings.effect: Median 48.4 vs 24.4 months; 19/44 vs 23/32 diagnosed.
findings.harms: Rash and temporary low lymphocyte counts; see the separate safety finding.
findings.limitation: A small trial in relatives. A group median cannot predict one person's delay.
findings.locator: Figure 1; Results → Efficacy
findings.population: 76 relatives with multiple islet autoantibodies and abnormal glucose tolerance, ages 8–49.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, one 14-day infusion course

findings.title: Skin reactions and low lymphocyte counts accompanied treatment
findings.summary: Skin events were more common with teplizumab. Most low lymphocyte counts resolved by day 45.
findings.followup: During active follow-up; blood counts tracked during recovery
findings.effect: Skin events: 16/44 vs 1/32. One participant's lymphocyte count normalized on day 105.
findings.uncertainty: Counts describe observed harms; rare-risk estimates are imprecise.
findings.harms: Rash; transient lymphopenia (low blood lymphocyte count).
findings.limitation: Safety event categories and individual symptoms are different units.
findings.locator: Table 2; Results → Safety
findings.population: 76 relatives with multiple islet autoantibodies and abnormal glucose tolerance, ages 8–49.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, one 14-day infusion course

findings.title: A longer look at the same people still found delay
findings.summary: More diagnoses accumulated in both groups. The extended analysis still favored teplizumab.
findings.effect: Median 59.6 vs 27.1 months; 22/44 vs 25/32 diagnosed.
findings.uncertainty: HR 0.457, p=0.01; interval not reported with Figure 1.
findings.harms: No new safety estimate extracted; consult the original TN-10 report.
findings.limitation: This updates the first trial's estimate. It adds observation time without adding an independent trial.
findings.locator: Figure 1; Results → extended follow-up
findings.population: 76 relatives with multiple islet autoantibodies and abnormal glucose tolerance, ages 8–49.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, one 14-day infusion course

findings.title: A T-cell change tracked with insulin secretion
findings.summary: A change in a CD8 T-cell subset correlated with a change in C-peptide, a marker of the body's own insulin production.
findings.endpoint: Change in KLRG1+ TIGIT+ memory CD8 cells versus change in C-peptide
findings.effect: Correlation r=0.44, p=0.014.
findings.uncertainty: An interval was not provided in the abstract.
findings.harms: Safety described in the primary TN-10 paper.
findings.limitation: The trial randomized the drug. It did not independently manipulate this cell subset, so mediation remains open.
findings.locator: Abstract; Results → C-peptide responses correlate with increases in partially exhausted CD8+ T cells
findings.population: 76 relatives with multiple islet autoantibodies and abnormal glucose tolerance, ages 8–49.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, one 14-day infusion course

findings.title: Protégé missed its clinical target
findings.summary: The full-dose arm and placebo had almost identical rates of simultaneously meeting the insulin and HbA1c targets.
findings.uncertainty: Design power was ~90% for 30% vs 5% response. A smaller effect remained possible.
findings.harms: Rash: 53% across teplizumab regimens vs 20% on placebo.
findings.limitation: Placebo response exceeded the design assumption. Later analyses were exploratory under the prespecified testing hierarchy.
findings.locator: Table 2; Statistical analysis → sample size and hierarchy
findings.population: 516 randomized, ages 8–35, diagnosed within 12 weeks. Efficacy analysis included 513 who received treatment.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, three regimens; two courses 26 weeks apart
findings.comparator: Placebo plus the same background diabetes care

findings.title: Less C-peptide loss in the full-dose arm
findings.summary: The year-two analysis favored full-dose teplizumab on a secondary endpoint. Some planned measurements had already stopped.
findings.endpoint: Change in meal-stimulated C-peptide on the log(AUC+1) scale
findings.effect: Adjusted changes −0.136 vs −0.191; difference +0.055 on the transformed scale.
findings.uncertainty: Nominal p=0.027. CI not tabulated in Table 1.
findings.harms: Grade ≥3 events at two years: 65.2% full-dose vs 28.6% placebo (Table 3).
findings.limitation: Only 64% of full-dose participants had year-two C-peptide. A secondary signal cannot reverse the primary result.
findings.locator: Table 1; Figure 1A; Results, first paragraph; safety Table 3
findings.population: 516 randomized, ages 8–35, diagnosed within 12 weeks. Efficacy analysis included 513 who received treatment.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, three regimens; two courses 26 weeks apart
findings.comparator: Placebo plus the same background diabetes care

findings.title: The antibody reached its T-cell target
findings.summary: Flow cytometry detected binding to CD3 and temporary changes in circulating T cells during dosing.
findings.effect: CD4 and CD8 counts fell transiently with teplizumab.
findings.uncertainty: Descriptive trajectories in Figure 3; no single pooled contrast extracted.
findings.harms: See Table 3 in this report.
findings.limitation: Target binding in blood cannot establish protection of pancreatic cells.
findings.locator: Figure 3A–C and accompanying text
findings.population: 516 randomized, ages 8–35, diagnosed within 12 weeks. Efficacy analysis included 513 who received treatment.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, three regimens; two courses 26 weeks apart
findings.comparator: Placebo plus the same background diabetes care

findings.title: A separate trial found greater insulin production after diagnosis
findings.summary: In PROTECT, children given teplizumab retained more of their own insulin production after diagnosis.
findings.endpoint: Change in stimulated C-peptide, log(AUC+1) after a 4-hour meal test
findings.effect: Adjusted difference +0.13 on the transformed C-peptide scale (article reports pmol/mL).
findings.harms: Reported events included rash, lymphopenia and mild cytokine release syndrome.
findings.limitation: Participants already had measurable secretion. This tests preservation, not regeneration.
findings.locator: Table 2, first row (intention to treat); Figure 1A
findings.population: 328 children ages 8–17, diagnosed within 6 weeks, with measurable stimulated C-peptide at entry.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, two 12-day infusion courses

findings.title: Less certain effects on daily diabetes management
findings.summary: The primary analysis did not detect differences in the key clinical endpoints. The insulin-use interval includes both benefit and little change.
findings.endpoint: Insulin use, HbA1c, time in range and clinically important hypoglycemia
findings.effect: Adjusted insulin-use difference −0.13 U/kg/day; time-in-range difference +4.71 percentage points.
findings.uncertainty: 95% CIs: −0.28 to +0.02 U/kg/day; −1.72 to +11.15 percentage points.
findings.harms: Infusion-related side effects; see source abstract.
findings.limitation: Week-78 insulin records were available for 98 treated and 50 placebo participants. Missing data matter.
findings.locator: Table 2, key secondary endpoints; Results
findings.population: 328 children ages 8–17, diagnosed within 6 weeks, with measurable stimulated C-peptide at entry.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, two 12-day infusion courses

findings.title: A selected PROTECT subgroup used less insulin
findings.summary: In participants who met the protocol criteria, daily insulin use was lower with teplizumab.
findings.effect: Adjusted difference −0.17 U/kg/day.
findings.harms: No separate harm estimate extracted for this selected comparison.
findings.limitation: Protocol-based exclusions occur after randomization. Compare with all 328 randomized participants before attributing a clinical effect.
findings.locator: Table 2; Study design and participants; Discussion
findings.population: 275 of the 328 PROTECT participants met the per-protocol criteria; 180 treated, 95 placebo. Ages 8–17.
findings.factor: Teplizumab, two 12-day infusion courses

findings.title: Transplanted cells produced a measurable meal response
findings.summary: C-peptide appeared after infusion in all 14 evaluated recipients. It was undetectable before treatment.
findings.population: Adults with recurrent severe hypoglycemia. Full-dose subset: 12 people, ages 24–60.
findings.factor: Stem cell–derived donor islets infused into the liver, with ongoing immune suppression.
findings.comparator: Each participant’s baseline; no concurrent control.
findings.endpoint: Meal-stimulated C-peptide, a measure of insulin secretion.
findings.effect: In the 12 full-dose recipients, average 90-minute C-peptide was 424 pmol/L on day 90 and 1,274 pmol/L on day 365.
findings.uncertainty: Small, uncontrolled interim analysis; uncertainty around differences from alternatives cannot be estimated here.
findings.harms: Systemic immune suppression continued. See the separate safety finding.
findings.limitation: Cell function alone does not establish the ability to stop insulin.
findings.locator: Abstract Results; full text, Efficacy, Figure 1A–B.

findings.title: Ten of twelve full-dose recipients were off insulin at one year
findings.summary: Two others still needed insulin, at lower doses. Everyone received anti-rejection medication.
findings.population: Adults with recurrent severe hypoglycemia. Full-dose subset: 12 people, ages 24–60.
findings.factor: Stem cell–derived donor islets infused into the liver, with ongoing immune suppression.
findings.comparator: Each participant’s baseline; no concurrent control.
findings.endpoint: Secondary endpoint: freedom from injected insulin. Primary Part C endpoint also included freedom from severe lows and HbA1c improvement.
findings.followup: Day 365; severe lows assessed on days 90–365.
findings.effect: 10/12 (83%) off insulin; remaining doses fell 70% and 36%. All 12 had no severe lows in the assessment window and HbA1c below 7%.
findings.uncertainty: Small, uncontrolled interim analysis; uncertainty around differences from alternatives cannot be estimated here.
findings.harms: Ongoing immune suppression.
findings.limitation: Durability after immune suppression stops was not tested.
findings.locator: Results, Efficacy, Table 1 and Figure 2B.

findings.title: Serious neutropenia and deaths occurred during follow-up
findings.summary: Three participants had serious neutropenia. Investigators attributed one fatal infection to immunosuppressive medication.
findings.population: Fourteen treated adults in the interim analysis, including two who received half doses.
findings.factor: Stem cell–derived donor islets infused into the liver, with ongoing immune suppression.
findings.followup: At least 12 months; deaths at approximately 19.5 and 30 months.
findings.effect: Three had serious neutropenia, two had serious acute kidney injury, and two died.
findings.uncertainty: Counts describe small, overlapping sets of people; causality differs by event.
findings.harms: One person died with cryptococcal meningitis after sinus surgery while taking high-dose steroids and immune suppression. The other death followed progression of existing neurocognitive disease.
findings.limitation: Investigators attributed no serious event to the cell product itself. Background drugs, procedures and cells were delivered together.
findings.locator: Results, Safety, following Table 2.

findings.title: The VX-264 device missed its insulin-production endpoint
findings.summary: The sponsor stopped advancing this product after day 90. The registry still listed the study as active and closed to recruitment.
findings.population: Adults eligible at 18–65 years with at least five years of T1D; seven enrolled across parts. Part B denominator undisclosed in the announcement.
findings.factor: Stem cell–derived islets inside a protective device.
findings.endpoint: Part B: change in peak meal-stimulated C-peptide. Safety was the other primary endpoint.
findings.followup: 90 days for efficacy; registry planned safety observation through 24 months.
findings.effect: Vertex described the C-peptide increase as insufficient. It gave no numerical change or confidence interval.
findings.uncertainty: The announcement omits the target threshold and participant-level responses.
findings.harms: Sponsor described overall tolerability favorably; event counts undisclosed.
findings.limitation: The result does not distinguish immune injury, poor survival or insufficient functional cell mass. Explant analyses were planned.
findings.locator: Vertex, March 28, 2025, VX-264 Update. Registry, Primary Outcome Measures.

findings.title: Anti-CD3 and donor islets were tested together in people
findings.summary: Four recipients stopped insulin through one year. The treatment included maintenance immune suppression.
findings.population: Six adults, ages 24–46, with absent baseline C-peptide and impaired awareness of low glucose.
findings.factor: hOKT3γ1(Ala-Ala) plus sirolimus started two days before donor-islet transplantation; sirolimus and low-dose tacrolimus continued.
findings.comparator: No arm received the same graft and maintenance drugs without anti-CD3.
findings.followup: One year planned; five of six completed follow-up.
findings.effect: 4/6 remained insulin independent through day 365; one retained partial function and one lost graft function at day 14.
findings.uncertainty: Six selected recipients. The added benefit of anti-CD3 cannot be estimated.
findings.harms: Three temporary severe neutropenia events and one temporary severe rash were reported across recipients.
findings.limitation: Donor preparation and multiple immune drugs changed together. This does not test stem cell–derived islets or withdrawal of maintenance therapy.
findings.locator: Results, Table 1 (age) and Table 3 (individual metabolic results).

findings.title: Gene-edited donor islets made insulin without systemic immune suppression
findings.summary: One recipient continued to use insulin while tests detected function of the transplanted cells.
findings.population: One 42-year-old man with 37 years of T1D and no measurable baseline C-peptide.
findings.factor: Edited donor islets implanted in forearm muscle, without immunosuppressants.
findings.endpoint: Glucose-responsive C-peptide and immune recognition of the edited cells.
findings.effect: C-peptide rose during meal tests at weeks 4, 8 and 12. Fasting levels were about 10 pmol/L; insulin injections continued.
findings.uncertainty: One person; no controlled estimate.
findings.harms: Four adverse events, none serious or judged related to the study product.
findings.limitation: Small graft dose and short observation. This case does not establish insulin independence or long-term safety.
findings.locator: Figure 3B–D and abstract, safety.

findings.title: The same graft showed evidence of function at 14 months
findings.summary: A later letter extended observation of the original recipient without systemic immune suppression.
findings.population: The same UP421 recipient as in the 2025 paper.
findings.factor: Follow-up of the same gene-edited graft.
findings.endpoint: Persistence of beta-cell function and detectable immune response against the graft.
findings.effect: The publisher summary reports evidence of continued function and no detected anti-graft response.
findings.uncertainty: Magnitude and assay thresholds were not verified from the full letter.
findings.harms: Detailed adverse-event follow-up unknown in the retrieved summary.
findings.limitation: One individual. Insulin independence is not established by this report.
findings.locator: Publisher summary of letter, first paragraph; DOI 10.1056/NEJMc2604408.

findings.title: A two-hour glucose test predicted progression across T1D cohorts
findings.population: TrialNet relatives, TEDDY children at inherited risk, Fr1da screening participants and DPT-1 relatives.
findings.factor: M120 progression risk score
findings.comparator: Five-sample Diabetes Prevention Trial Risk Score and other time-point models.
findings.followup: Median follow-up varied by analysis group from 1.8 to 3.1 years.
findings.effect: Validation AUC was 0.745 in TrialNet, 0.865 in TEDDY, 0.742 in Fr1da and 0.694 in DPT-1.
findings.uncertainty: See the cohort comparison for 95% intervals. Fr1da had 80 participants.
findings.harms: Observational prediction analysis.
findings.limitation: Recruitment and measurement schedules differed. Discrimination alone cannot establish an individual’s absolute risk.
findings.summary: Researchers developed a progression score in TrialNet relatives and tested it in several populations. Its ability to distinguish later diagnosis varied across cohorts.
findings.locator: Population and follow-up in Table 1. Model estimates in Tables 2 and 3.

families.name: DAISY, DIPP and German birth cohorts
families.outcome: Autoantibody profiles and HLA predicted later diagnosis in genetically susceptible children.
families.status: Published pooled analysis with follow-up through July 2012.
families.subsequent: Later follow-up of these children was outside this extraction.
families.replication: Three geographic cohorts contributed. Ten-year risks after multiple antibodies were 70.8% in Colorado, 71.9% in Finland and 61.7% in Germany. These estimates share the pooled publication.

families.name: Coppieters donor pancreas series
families.outcome: Some islets contained antigen-reactive CD8 cells; pathology varied across donors and regions.
families.status: Published cross-sectional tissue series. No intervention or trial status.
families.subsequent: The index includes one report from this specimen series.
families.replication: Multiple sections from one pancreas are repeated measurements. Independent replication of the specific staining result has not been adjudicated here.

families.name: TEDDY birth cohort
families.outcome: Persistent EV-B shedding was associated with autoimmunity; the analysis of clinical T1D was less conclusive.
families.status: Observational birth cohort with a published nested case-control analysis. Administrative status was not abstracted for this edition.
families.subsequent: NIDDK lists a version 35 dataset available by request. The catalog supplies metadata only.
families.replication: The endpoint samples overlap. The data catalog describes the same cohort.

families.name: Faulkner virome evidence review
families.outcome: Three stool studies contributed to a pooled association between consecutive shedding and islet autoimmunity.
families.status: Published systematic review of observational studies.
families.subsequent: Review-level follow-up was outside this extraction.
families.replication: Vehik’s TEDDY sample is included. The pooled measure uses a broader exposure definition than the same-strain estimate.

families.name: Skowera human islet coculture
families.outcome: A selected CD8 clone killed HLA-compatible human islet cells in vitro.
families.subsequent: The independent donor series used staining to ask a different question.
families.replication: Coppieters examined cells inside donor tissue. Its observations complement the culture assay but do not repeat the killing experiment.

families.name: TrialNet TN-10
families.outcome: A single course of anti-CD3 delayed clinical diagnosis in high-risk relatives.
families.status: Registry: completed, June 2019. The registered primary measure was the annual rate of new diabetes diagnoses.
families.subsequent: Sims and colleagues followed the original randomized groups for longer.
families.replication: Same trial in both papers. This collection contains no independent repeat of the stage 2 diagnosis-delay endpoint.

families.name: Protégé
families.outcome: The one-year combined glucose-control and insulin-use target was missed. Subsequent C-peptide data favored full-dose treatment.
families.status: Registry: completed, August 2011. Hagopian et al. (2013, Methods) report that after the year-one miss, follow-up continued but selected lab measurements ceased to reduce cost and participant burden.
families.subsequent: PROTECT later made C-peptide its primary endpoint in newly diagnosed children. It did not repeat the Protégé composite.
families.replication: The two Protégé papers share a cohort. PROTECT used separate participants and had some overlapping investigators.

families.name: PROTECT
families.outcome: The pediatric trial met its C-peptide target. Clinical secondary endpoints were inconclusive in the original randomized comparison.
families.status: Registry: completed May 1, 2023. Primary measure: change in meal-stimulated C-peptide to week 78.
families.subsequent: A 2026 paper reanalyzed participants meeting protocol criteria and found lower insulin use in this subset.
families.replication: A different trial from Protégé, with different ages, dosing and endpoints. Its 2026 analysis uses a subset of PROTECT participants.

families.name: FORWARD • NCT04786262
families.outcome: Insulin production returned and 10/12 full-dose recipients were insulin independent at one year with ongoing immunosuppression.
families.status: Interim report from an ongoing multiphase study. The master protocol now includes a second cell product.
families.subsequent: On Nov 2, 2026 Vertex announced that it would prioritize VX-017, intended to reach more blood types. That decision is not an efficacy result for either product.
families.replication: One study. The registry and interim publication describe the same protocol; the other graft studies used different products.

families.name: VX-264 • NCT05791201
families.outcome: Day-90 insulin production fell short of the sponsor’s efficacy criterion.
families.status: The registry snapshot posted Sept 10, 2026 listed active, not recruiting, with seven enrolled.
families.subsequent: On March 28, 2025 Vertex stopped advancing VX-264 and announced plans to study explanted devices. Mechanistic results of those analyses are unknown here.
families.replication: One device study. Zimislecel uses another delivery and protection strategy.

families.name: Minnesota donor-islet pilot
families.outcome: Four of six recipients stopped insulin for the first year on a multi-drug transplant regimen.
families.status: Planned one-year follow-up; five completed it. One person withdrew after losing graft function.
families.subsequent: A subsequent Minnesota protocol, NCT00265473, describes the pilot and enrolled five recipients under an extension protocol.
families.replication: A subsequent protocol at the same center does not independently replicate an anti-CD3-specific effect.

families.name: Minnesota extension • NCT00265473
families.outcome: The design tests the combined regimen and follows up the original pilot.
families.status: Completed. The registry reports actual enrollment of five.
families.subsequent: Separate follow-on protocol. Outcomes in its description for the original six refer to the earlier pilot.
families.replication: Same team, subsequent protocol. No randomized estimate of the antibody’s added benefit.

families.name: Teplizumab terminology
families.outcome: The FDA lists hOKT3γ1(Ala-Ala), MGA031 and PRV-031 as names for teplizumab.
families.status: Regulatory document, not a participant cohort.
families.subsequent: The terminology connects later progression studies with the 2004 donor-islet paper.
families.replication: Drug-name mapping supplies no new efficacy observation.

families.name: UP421 • Uppsala graft case
families.outcome: Insulin secretion was detectable after implantation without systemic immune suppression. The recipient still needed insulin at 12 weeks.
families.status: The 2025 report covers 12 weeks. Overall trial status is outside the case report.
families.subsequent: In 2026 the same team reported further observations through month 14.
families.replication: Two reports about one person. Longer observation increases follow-up but adds no independent recipient.

families.name: TrialNet, TEDDY, Fr1da and DPT-1 progression study
families.outcome: A two-hour glucose test helped distinguish future progression across cohorts.
families.subsequent: The paper reports subgroup tests and comparisons with multi-sample scores.
families.replication: Several populations were evaluated in one paper. The single-antibody analysis partly reused TrialNet participants.
